what: Cboe Global Markets runs options, futures and stock exchanges. Its most valuable products are options on the S&P 500 index and the VIX volatility index, which it owns and which trade nowhere else.
customers: Options and futures traders, market makers, brokers, asset managers and data subscribers.
money: S&P 500 index options, VIX products and equity options
Europe and Asia Pacific, Futures, FX
moat: Exclusive licences to trade options on the S&P 500 and ownership of the VIX, which cannot be replicated by a competing exchange.
risks: Trading volumes fall in calm markets
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
Index licence agreements must be renewed
Competition for equity trading market share is intense
opportunities: Revenue grew about 15% last year with a 31% operating margin
Retail participation in index options has grown sharply, including same-day expiries
Data and access subscriptions grow regardless of trading volumes
watch: Index options volumes and data and access revenue growth.
